questionText: Which of the following is a key obligation of a public procurement officer under Ethiopian law?
options: Ensuring that contracts are always awarded to local suppliers
Acting impartially, following prescribed procedures, and protecting public interest
Approving all procurement requests from their department
Selecting suppliers based on their past relationship with the organization

questionText: What is the primary difference between "open" and "restricted" tendering?
options: Open tendering is used for services while restricted tendering is for goods
Open tendering allows any eligible supplier to bid while restricted tendering limits invitations to a pre-selected group
Open tendering has no minimum bid validity period
Restricted tendering always results in a lower contract price than open tendering

questionText: Which of the following is a key challenge in public procurement in Ethiopia?
options: Excessive number of registered suppliers
Capacity gaps in procurement staff, limited transparency, and delayed procurement cycles
Over-reliance on international competitive bidding
Too many procurement regulations limiting flexibility

questionText: What is the significance of a "performance bond" in a government works contract?
options: It pays the contractor in advance for mobilization costs
It provides financial assurance that the contractor will complete the project as agreed
It guarantees that the government will pay the contractor on time
It exempts the contractor from penalty clauses in the contract

questionText: Which of the following factors must be considered when evaluating bids for a consultancy service?
options: The number of staff employed by the consulting firm
Technical competence, relevant experience, and proposed methodology
The geographic proximity of the firm to the procuring entity
The number of countries in which the firm has offices

questionText: Which of the following is the best approach to promoting sustainable procurement in the public sector?
options: Choosing only the cheapest supplier regardless of environmental performance
Incorporating environmental and social criteria into procurement specifications and evaluation
Restricting procurement to locally produced goods regardless of quality
Eliminating supplier evaluation criteria related to social responsibility

questionText: What is meant by "procurement cycle time"?
options: The number of procurement activities completed in a fiscal year
The total time taken from identifying a procurement need to contract award and delivery
The time required for the PPAA to approve a procurement plan
The duration of the bid validity period

questionText: In government procurement, what is the purpose of issuing an addendum to bidding documents?
options: To inform the winning bidder of contract conditions
To communicate changes or clarifications to all bidders before the submission deadline
To extend the bid validity period after bids are received
To notify unsuccessful bidders of their disqualification

questionText: Which of the following best describes "competitive negotiation" as a procurement method?
options: A method where prices are negotiated secretly with a single supplier
A method where proposals are solicited and negotiations conducted with the most technically suitable offers
A method reserved exclusively for procurement of IT systems
A method used when the budget is insufficient for open tendering

questionText: What is the ethical obligation of a procurement officer who discovers irregularities in a colleague's procurement activity?
options: Ignore the matter to avoid workplace conflict
Report the irregularity to the appropriate authority following established procedures
Confront the colleague directly without involving management
Document the irregularity privately without reporting it

questionText: Which of the following is a key feature of e-procurement systems in government?
options: They allow procurement to be conducted without any documentation
They automate and digitize procurement processes, improving transparency and efficiency
They restrict procurement to suppliers registered outside Ethiopia
They eliminate the requirement for bid security in all procurement

questionText: What is the most important outcome of effective contract management in the public sector?
options: Minimizing the number of contract amendments
Ensuring that suppliers deliver the agreed goods or services on time, within budget, and to specification
Reducing the number of future procurement activities
Maximizing the number of suppliers retained for future contracts

questionText: Which of the following is a fundamental requirement for a valid government procurement contract?
options: A verbal agreement between the procuring entity and the supplier
A written document signed by both parties, clearly defining rights, obligations, and deliverables
Approval from all unsuccessful bidders before signing
Submission of the contract to the PPAA before it takes effect

questionText: What does "procurement audit" primarily aim to achieve?
options: To negotiate better prices with existing suppliers
To assess whether procurement activities comply with applicable laws and achieve value for money
To develop annual procurement plans for the next fiscal year
To certify the financial statements of the procuring entity

questionText: Which of the following is a legitimate use of the "emergency procurement" method?
options: Procuring office furniture because the fiscal year is ending
Procuring life-saving medicines in response to an unexpected disease outbreak
Procuring vehicles to replace those that were regularly maintained
Procuring construction materials for a project planned over a year ago

questionText: What is a key advantage of centralizing procurement in a government organization?

It achieves economies of scale, reduces duplication, and strengthens oversight
It eliminates the need for technical specifications
It ensures that procurement is completed without competitive bidding

questionText: Which of the following best describes "specifications by performance" in procurement?
options: Specifying the exact brand and model of the product required
Describing the functional outcomes required without prescribing how to achieve them
Providing a sample of the product that all bidders must match exactly
Listing the chemical composition of the required product in detail

questionText: In public procurement, what does "best evaluated bid" mean?
options: The bid with the absolute lowest price
The bid that offers the best combination of technical compliance and evaluated cost
The bid submitted first before all others
The bid with the most attractive packaging and presentation

questionText: Which of the following is an obligation of the procuring entity regarding bid confidentiality?
options: Publishing all bid prices on the government website before the bid opening date
Keeping bid contents confidential until the official bid opening to protect the integrity of the process
Sharing bid prices with all participants before submission to promote competition
Informing each bidder of the prices submitted by competitors after evaluation

questionText: What distinguishes "supply" from "procurement" in the public sector context?
options: Supply involves sourcing while procurement involves delivery only
Procurement is the process of acquiring goods and services while supply encompasses the broader management of material flow into and within the organization
Supply is a government-specific term while procurement applies only to the private sector

questionText: Which of the following is the most effective way to reduce procurement risks in the public sector?

Applying thorough planning, following due process, and maintaining strong oversight mechanisms
Limiting procurement to a few trusted long-term suppliers
Delegating all procurement decisions to a single procurement officer

questionText: What is the purpose of establishing a "supplier blacklist" in government procurement?
options: To give advantage to local suppliers over foreign competitors
To prevent suppliers found guilty of fraud, poor performance, or corruption from participating in future procurement
To reduce the number of suppliers competing in each tender

questionText: Which of the following situations would most justify the use of "request for quotations"?
options: Procurement of a hospital construction project worth 50 million ETB
Procurement of low-value, standardized goods readily available in the market
Procurement of specialized consulting services for policy development
Procurement of complex military equipment requiring technical evaluation

questionText: What is the significance of the "standstill period" between contract award notification and contract signing?

It provides a window for unsuccessful bidders to submit complaints before the contract is finalized

questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of maintaining a comprehensive procurement records management system?

questionText: What does "equal treatment of bidders" require in government procurement?

questionText: Which of the following is the main reason why procurement planning is linked to budgeting in the public sector?

To align procurement activities with available funding and prevent unauthorized expenditure
To reduce the number of items procured during the fiscal year

questionText: What is the primary risk of accepting unsolicited proposals in government procurement?

questionText: In Ethiopian public procurement, which document is used to formally notify the winning bidder of the contract award before signing?
options: The performance security form
The letter of acceptance or notification of award
The bid evaluation summary report

questionText: Which of the following best defines "public interest" as a guiding principle in government procurement?
options: Maximizing the profit of the procuring entity
Ensuring that procurement decisions serve the broader needs of citizens and society efficiently and ethically
